name: philips
category: consumer electronics manufacturer brand site (no cart, not a retailer)
reason: philips.sa is Philips N.V.'s own regional consumer-electronics marketing/information site for Saudi Arabia -- product categories, registration and newsletter sign-up, but no pricing, cart, or checkout anywhere. It is a manufacturer's brand site, not a retail storefront.

name: basp
reason: Babalghoum Auto Spare Parts is an automotive parts business (American car parts, classic and modern) -- explicit Gate-2 hard-fail category, and the site itself is a contact/brochure page (phone + WhatsApp only) with no cart.

name: AstraZeneca
category: pharmaceutical manufacturer HCP professional portal (not retail)
reason: azedugate.com is AstraZeneca's login-gated professional/medical portal for healthcare professionals across the Gulf and Saudi Arabia -- therapy-area content, screening tools, adverse-event reporting -- with zero consumer commerce. Not a retail business in any approved category.

name: invntec
category: 3D-printing / reverse-engineering specialist services and niche equipment reseller
reason: INVNTEC self-describes as an engineering/technology enterprise built around 3D-printing and reverse-engineering SERVICES, with an 'INVNTEC Store' selling 3D printers/materials/spare parts as a narrow, low-repeat-purchase adjunct. This is a specialist B2B-leaning technical services and niche-equipment business, not a general consumer retail operation in an approved category.

name: al-kadi
category: automotive/truck spare parts distribution (B2B wholesale + automotive parts)
reason: Al-Kadi Commerce & Industry Co. is a large-scale truck/trailer/passenger-vehicle spare-parts distributor (44K+ SKUs, vendor/supplier program, OEM brand partnerships) -- doubly hard-excluded as both automotive parts and B2B wholesale/distribution, despite being a genuine, substantial, Saudi-HQ'd (Dammam) operation with a real e-store.

name: jnini
reason: Salla-hosted store confirmed to sell ONLY diapers. Sitemap enumeration shows exactly 27 total product URLs, every single one a diaper pack (two brands, Jnini and Baby Time, sizes 1-6, in economic/small-box/big-box/colored-box configurations) with zero other product types (no wipes, baby food, clothing, etc). This is a single narrow product line, and independently falls well below the 50-SKU scale floor.

name: tefal
category: cookware & home appliances (global manufacturer's branded subsidiary storefront)
reason: tefal.sa is the official regional storefront of Tefal, operated per its own legal notice by 'Group SEB Arabia for home appliances,' the KSA-registered branch of Groupe SEB. The operating entity's global HQ is Groupe SEB, headquartered in Ecully, France -- not Saudi Arabia. This is a multinational manufacturer's own branded subsidiary storefront, not an independently Saudi-HQ'd retail company (the 'store run by a foreign-HQ'd group' failure pattern, not the franchise-operator carve-out).

name: nukhbatech
reason: Genuine Riyadh, Saudi Arabia-HQ'd e-commerce retailer (PrestaShop) confirmed via direct server-rendered fetch: real per-unit SAR checkout (cart/wishlist/compare), spanning CCTV cameras (Hikvision, EZVIZ, Dahua), smart TVs, dash cams, smart locks, access-control/attendance devices, and gate/barrier systems -- multiple distinct consumer-facing product families, not a single narrow line. 25+ distinct SKUs visible on the homepage sample alone across many sub-categories/brand lines, comfortably clearing the 50-SKU substantiality floor once the full catalog (additional category pages) is considered. || CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent 2nd pass): Real Riyadh tech store, but Gate 2 hybrid-B2B is unresolved: catalog leans on business-oriented lines (access-control, attendance devices, gate/barrier systems) alongside consumer items, and the site now returns 403 with search budget exhausted, so pure-B2C status and the inferred (never actually counted) 50-SKU scale can't be confirmed either way.

name: novonordisk
reason: novonordisk.com.sa is Novo Nordisk's own corporate/regulatory site for Saudi Arabia. Novo Nordisk's global HQ is Bagsvaerd, Denmark; the KSA site is the manufacturer's own subsidiary presence, not a Saudi-HQ'd company. Independently also fails as a pharma manufacturer (Gate 2) and has zero e-commerce -- prescription-only medicines that the site explicitly says are not advertised or sold to the public (Gate 4).

name: mro
reason: mro.sa is the 'Saudi MRO Marketplace,' a B2B marketplace for industrial Maintenance-Repair-Overhaul parts/services, with a 'Made in Saudi Arabia' zero-margin/zero-fee program plus free technical engineering for local manufacturers. This is industrial/wholesale trade infrastructure, not consumer retail -- a hard-fail under Gate 2 (wholesale/trading/distribution, industrial).

name: nazih
reason: Nazih is a genuine large beauty/cosmetics retail chain with 50-99 Saudi showrooms (Riyadh, Al Hofuf, Medina, Mushait, Najran, Tabuk) and 1000-4999 local staff -- but it is the Saudi retail arm of Nazih Group, founded in 1975 in Beirut, Lebanon by Nazih Hamad, with manufacturing units in Lebanon/UAE/UK and a presence across 21 MENA countries plus Europe and Canada. The operating entity's global HQ is Beirut, Lebanon, not Saudi Arabia. Per the geography rule, extensive real local operations do not override a foreign global HQ.

name: myesuq
reason: myesuq.com is a real registered business (Soqi Ana for Trade LLC, Riyadh, CR 1010772668) selling women's abayas/thobes/fashion, cosmetics, and perfumes via a marketplace model, with a dedicated Google Play app. However the live site is consistently unreachable: repeated curl and WebFetch attempts across multiple retries (including different paths and longer timeouts) all returned Cloudflare 522 (origin connection timed out) or hard connection timeouts, with no successful page load. No alternate live domain was found. Checked for an app-download rescue given its marketplace/app nature, but found no confirmed install-count evidence (no 50k+ signal). Per Gate 4, a persistently unreachable domain with no live site findable and no rescue evidence fails.

name: qvskincareme
reason: qvskincareme.com is QV Skincare's own Middle East regional site (QV is a brand of Ego Pharmaceuticals, headquartered in Australia) -- a country-selection splash page (Bahrain/Jordan/Kuwait/Oman/Qatar/UAE/KSA), not an independently Gulf-HQ'd retail company. This fails Gate 1 as a multinational manufacturer's own regional brand portal rather than a local retailer.

name: roos
reason: roos.sa does not resolve at all (NXDOMAIN via both system DNS and a direct Python socket lookup) -- a genuinely dead domain, not merely blocked or slow. Targeted WebSearch for the domain and plausible Arabic-name variants returned no business matching this name anywhere; no alternate live domain was identifiable, and there was no signal of an app/marketplace nature to justify an app-download-rescue search. Fails Gate 4 as a dead/unreachable domain with no live site findable anywhere.

name: circleall
reason: CircleAll is explicitly an automotive parts marketplace/store ('Select Your Vehicle,' 'Over 120,000 Automotive and Truck Parts,' 'Sell On CircleAll') covering Auto Parts, Engine, Brakes, Filters, Suspension, Air Conditioning, Tires, Lights, Transmission, Oil & Grease, Electrics, Tools, Steering, Wipers, and Body. Automotive parts/tires are an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category.

name: zameter
reason: Zameter sells marble, quartz, and porcelain surfacing materials for kitchen countertops, bathroom walls/sinks, and wall cladding, explicitly targeting homeowners as well as architects, designers, and contractors, with dedicated business accounts at discounted rates and a 'request a quote' sales model. This is construction/surfacing-material supply, an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail (building materials/construction), reinforced by its B2B/contractor-oriented sales model.

name: osco
reason: Osco Investment Company describes itself as specializing in 'contracting (construction) and digital marketing/services,' covering construction of residential/commercial/industrial buildings, roads, and mechanical/electrical works, plus PR/digital-marketing agency services. Both construction/contracting and B2B agency services are explicit Gate 2 hard-fail categories; the site has no products or e-commerce at all, only a consultation-booking form.

name: pfizermedicalinformation
reason: This is Pfizer's own official medical-information portal for Saudi Arabia healthcare professionals and patients (adverse-event reporting, medical inquiries). Pfizer's global HQ is New York, USA; the site is the manufacturer's own regional regulatory presence, not a Saudi-HQ'd company, and independently has zero retail/e-commerce functionality.

name: ictc
category: building materials (construction hardware: nails, wire, rebar)
reason: ICTC explicitly identifies itself as 'مورد مواد البناء في السعودية' (building materials supplier in Saudi Arabia), selling nails, galvanized/PVC/welding wire, rebar, chain-link/barbed-wire fencing, and welded mesh, and explicitly advertises 'wholesale and trade prices.' This is construction-hardware wholesale/trade supply, an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category, despite being a real, live, substantial e-commerce operation.

name: redasafe
reason: REDA Safe sells PPE, firefighting gear and industrial/workplace safety supplies to companies across industries -- a B2B industrial-supplies business, not any approved consumer retail category.

name: calvinklein

The real operating group's HQ is the UAE, the same pattern as the confirmed Dyson/Chalhoub case in this batch.

name: dezigndistrict
reason: A real, live luxury furniture e-commerce store with a Riyadh showroom, named products, warranty and free-shipping policy -- but it is explicitly 'Part of Indospace Group,' whose headquarters, production and distribution are confirmed to be in Central Java, Indonesia, not Saudi Arabia.

name: yves-rocher
reason: The domain is dead: DNS does not resolve (confirmed via two independent network paths) and every HTTP/HTTPS variant tried failed. No live replacement domain was found; the brand now appears reachable only via third-party marketplaces (Noon, Amazon.sa), not its own transactional site.
